title_en: Japan clarifies nationality evidence for septic-tank manager certificate applications in 2026

quick_take.what_changed: Environment Ministry Ordinance No. 23 of 2026 amended Articles 15 and 18 of the Enforcement Regulation under the Septic Tank Act to expressly recognize resident-record entries showing nationality or equivalent particulars for people without Japanese nationality. It took effect on 31 August 2026.
quick_take.who_is_affected: Applicants for septic-tank manager certificates and holders seeking a replacement certificate after a change in recorded particulars, especially applicants without Japanese nationality.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: Check the documentary evidence required by the applicable application form. For a non-Japanese national, the revised provisions expressly refer to a resident record stating nationality or equivalent particulars. Existing forms are subject to transitional rules.

instruments.name_en: Ordinance Partially Amending the Enforcement Regulation under the Septic Tank Act

watch_pages.label: e-Gov current regulation and revision history

paragraphs: The septic-tank manager certificate application procedure is governed by Article 15 of the ministerial regulation, which implements the certificate framework in Article 45(1) of the Septic Tank Act. Applicants must submit the prescribed application and supporting documents to the Minister of the Environment.

Earlier Article 15 and Article 18 procedures already allowed a family-register extract, a resident record showing registered domicile, or equivalent documentary evidence. An Environment Ministry circular dated 28 September 2001 expressly identified an alien-registration certificate as an example of substitute evidence. The 2026 amendment expressly refers to a resident record showing nationality or equivalent particulars for a person without Japanese nationality. It must not be characterized as the first recognition of documentary alternatives for foreign applicants; nor does it itself establish new certificate eligibility or waive examination or training requirements.

The text is consistent with clarifying how the procedure works for applicants who do not have a Japanese registered domicile. That policy rationale is an inference from the amendment, not a verified quotation from the ministry's explanation.

The historical baseline is important: the Environment Ministry's 28 September 2001 circular explained that substitute identity documents could already be used for issuance and replacement applications under Articles 15 and 18, including the then-existing alien-registration certificate. That circular concerns the 2001 regime and does not itself state the purpose of the 2026 amendment.

A draft was opened for public comment in July 2026. The e-Gov results record identifies the final instrument as Environment Ministry Ordinance No. 23 of 2026, promulgated on 31 August 2026 and effective the same day. The amendment changes Article 15 on certificate issuance and Article 18 on certificate replacement.

Article 15 continues to require the prescribed application and supporting documents. Article 18 continues to permit, rather than compel, a certificate holder to seek replacement after recorded particulars change.

confirmed.text: The revised documentary wording applies from 31 August 2026.

Existing documents using the former forms are deemed to use the revised forms under supplementary provision paragraph 2; paragraph 3 permits existing old-form paper to be adapted and used for the time being.

uncertainties: The ministry's 2001 circular confirms that substitute evidence predated the 2026 amendment, but does not establish the ministry's specific policy rationale in 2026. That rationale and any current administrative instructions require separate confirmation.
The amendment does not itself demonstrate that certificate eligibility, examination requirements, or substantive qualification criteria changed.

paragraphs: Applicants without Japanese nationality and employers assisting with applications should update their documentation checklist to reflect the express nationality-entry alternative, while confirming the current form and any guidance from the competent authority.

Training organizations and administrative staff should distinguish the mandatory supporting-document submission for initial issuance from the optional replacement application when certificate particulars change. The transitional provisions reduce disruption for existing documents and old printed forms.
checklist: Identify whether the filing concerns initial issuance under Article 15 or replacement under Article 18.
Check whether a resident record with nationality or equivalent particulars is appropriate for an applicant without Japanese nationality.
Verify the currently prescribed form and required examination or course-completion evidence; do not infer any relaxation of qualification requirements.
Apply the supplementary provisions correctly when handling pre-amendment forms and existing paperwork.
